content.text: Direct comparisons between feedback sources remain sparse. An earlier naturalistic case study found teacher feedback addressed more error types (16) than automated feedback (8), though assignment differences may have confounded this comparison (Zhang & Hyland, 2018). Zhang and Hyland (2021) reported that students in an authentic classroom spent more time revising after automated feedback (6.2 hours) than after peer feedback (5.8 hours) or teacher feedback (4.7 hours), and that the integration of the three types—rather than any single source—appeared to facilitate active engagement. Engagement was uneven: some students responded with indifference, viewing the revision cycle as overkill (Zhang & Hyland, 2021).
